summary_html: Agency chooses **Differential Response (DR)**/**Alternative Response**: engage **services without court petition** when safety permits. FFPSA and IV-B/IV-E prevention funding support voluntary, front-end help to avert removals.
authority_html:
- **Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA)** — prevention services framework under IV-E  
- **SSA Title IV-B & IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m; 670–679c)** — service funding & case-plan requirements  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — assesses safety/permanency outcomes in DR systems

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed reversal of a termination judgment, holding that where reunification is the permanent plan the department must make reasonable efforts to help the parent remove the impediments to reunification - here to obtain suitable and affordable housing - before seeking termination under La. Ch.C. art. 1015(5).
key_cases.relevance: Supports resolving a poverty-driven family crisis with services rather than an escalating court track.
key_cases.quote: the duty to make reasonable efforts to remove the impediments to reunification does not necessarily stop once the children are removed from the parent's custody

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the reasonable-efforts requirement of 42 U.S.C. section 671(a)(15) confers no privately enforceable right under section 1983 and creates no implied private cause of action, leaving enforcement to the Secretary's funding-review machinery.
key_cases.relevance: Means a family denied front-end prevention services cannot sue to compel them under Title IV-E; the remedy is state-law and administrative.
key_cases.quote: the "reasonable efforts" language does not unambiguously confer an enforceable right upon the Act's beneficiaries

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court held the juvenile court exceeded its authority by ordering the department to move a child adjudicated in need of care into a certified foster home, because La. Ch.C. art. 672(A) gives the department sole authority over placement, with judicial control exercised through approval and review of the case plan.
key_cases.relevance: Locates judicial leverage in case-plan approval and review rather than in direct command of the agency's service choices.
key_cases.quote: the court was without authority to order the child's movement to a certified foster home

state_agency.name: Louisiana Department of Children and Family Services

investigation_requirements: DCFS investigates only where the suspected perpetrator is a parent or caretaker as defined in La. Ch.C. Art. 603 or falls within one of the additional categories in Art. 610(A)(1) (a person in an interpersonal dating or engagement relationship with the parent or caretaker, a person living in the same residence as the parent or caretaker or in any residence of the child, an early learning center or registered family child day care home operator or employee, another child residing in the same residence in a case of suspected sexual abuse, or an indeterminable perpetrator where the abuse is suspected to have occurred at the child’s residence); every other report is routed to a local or state law enforcement agency (La. Ch.C. Art. 610(A)(1)-(2))

In lieu of an investigation, reports of low levels of risk may be assessed through interviews with the family to identify needs and available matches to community resources; if the assessment shows the child is at immediate substantial risk of harm, the local child protection unit must immediately conduct an intensive investigation (La. Ch.C. Art. 612(A)(3))

Reports of sexual abuse in which the alleged perpetrator is a child may be assessed immediately through interviews with the family of the child victim and the alleged child perpetrator rather than investigated, with the same immediate-intensive-investigation trigger (La. Ch.C. Art. 612(A)(4); see also Art. 610(G)(5))
